recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13997 unless Patient Care approves a new change request with concrete use cases that reverses the 2025 no-change decision on adding unknown.
issue_request: FHIR-13997 was a Published STU3 Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus support unknown/default handling because the STU3 element was mandatory and some systems did not know whether an allergy was confirmed, unconfirmed, or refuted. The accepted resolution was to make AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus 0..1 rather than add an unknown code.
initial_application: Commit 52ac1cc0e7288f26eca9df7e2fb559dcbcbc1efd explicitly referenced #13997 and changed the then-authoritative AllergyIntolerance spreadsheet cardinality for AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus from 1..1 to 0..1. Later source refactors regenerated or migrated that content into the current StructureDefinition XML and terminology files.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current StructureDefinition has verificationStatus min 0/max 1 with a required binding and no unknown in the displayed code list. The 2017 Zulip thread linked from Jira records the STU3 interoperability problem and notes GF#13997 would relax cardinality. A later R6 core request, FHIR-47613, again proposed adding unknown, but Patient Care resolved it Not Persuasive/No Change after a failed motion to add unknown, supporting no current source edit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source files were changed because the current build-scope source already reflects the seed decision and later Patient Care evidence argues against adding unknown now.
